questions.q_en: In a 5-km race, A beats B by 750 metres and C by 1260 metres. By how many metres does B beat C in the same race?
questions.solution_en:
Let B beat C by T metres.

Length of race course = Distance covered by A = 5 km = 5000 m

Distance covered by B = 5000 - 750 = 4250 m

Distance covered by C = 5000 - 1260 = 3740 m

And

Distance covered by B = 5000 m

Distance covered by C = 5000 - T m

Now,

5000/(5000 - T) = 4250/3740

5000 - T = 4400

T = 600 m

questions.q_en: In a 100-m race, A beats B by 20 m and B beats C by 5 m. In the same race, find the distance by which A beats C.
questions.solution_en:
Ratio of speeds of A and B = 100 : 80 = 5 : 4

Ratio of speeds of B and C = 100 : 95 = 20 : 19

Ratio of speeds of A and C = 5/4 * 20/19 = 25/19

When A runs 100 m, C runs (19/25) * 100 = 76 m

A beats C by = 100 - 76 = 24 m

questions.q_en:
P and Q take part in 400 m race. P runs at 12 km/hr. P gives Q a start of 20 m and still beats him by 13 seconds. The speed of Q is:

(Round up to two decimal places.)
questions.solution_en:
Time taken by P to complete the race = (400/1000)/(12) = 1/30 hours

Time taken by Q to complete the race = 1/30 + 13/3600 = 133/3600 hours

Distance covered by Q = 400 - 20 = 380 m = 0.38 km

Speed of Q = 0.38/(133/3600) = 10.29 km/hr
questions.solution_hi:

Speed of Q = 0.38/(133/3600) = 10.29 km/hr

Vishu's speed as V m/s

Vishu's speed in the first race;

Equating the two speeds:

765/ Ta +20=711/Ta+8

Multiply both sides by (Ta + 20)(Ta +8) to eliminate the denominators;

765(Ta+8)=711(Ta+20)

Expanding both sides;

765Ta+6120=711Ta+14220

Now, subtract 711T_a from both sides:

765Ta-711Ta=14220-6120

Ta= 150 seconds

Atul takes 150 seconds to run the full race.

Now, let's find Vishu's time:

Using the equation for Vishu's speed in the first race:

765/ Ta+20=765/150+20=765/170=4.5m/sec

Vishu's speed:V=4.5m/s

questions.q_en: Arun and Bhaskar run a race of 3 km. First, Arun gives Bhaskar a head start of 400 m and beats him by 30 seconds. While coming back, Arun gives Bhaskar a lead of 2.5 minutes and gets beaten by 500 m. What is the difference between the times in minutes in which Arun and Bhaskar can run the race for one side separately?
questions.solution_en:
Let:

Arun's speed = A m/s

Bhaskar's speed = B m/s

Race distance = 3000 m

First Scenario:

Bhaskar runs 2600 m (3000 - 400).

Let T be the time (in seconds) for Arun to run 3000 m: A = 3000/T.

Bhaskar takes (T + 30) seconds to finish 2600 m: B = 2600/(T + 30).

Second Scenario:

Bhaskar gets a 2.5-minute (150 s) lead.

Bhaskar's time for 3000 m: x = 3000/B.

Arun runs for (x - 150) seconds and covers 2500 m: A(x - 150) = 2500.

Substituting the expressions for A and B from the first scenario leads to T = 360 s.

Thus, speeds:

A = 3000/360 = 25/3 m/s,

B = 2600/390 = 20/3 m/s.

Times for 3000 m:

Arun: 3000/(25/3) = 360 s = 6 min

Bhaskar: 3000/(20/3) = 450 s = 7.5 min

Difference = 450 - 360 = 90 s = 1.5 min

Option(b) is the correct answer

questions.q_en: In an 800 m race, the ratio of the speeds of two contestants Ankur and Neha is 5:6. If Ankur has a head-start of 200 m, then Ankur will win by
questions.solution_en:
Speeds: Ankur:Neha = 5:6

Ankur runs 600 m (800-200), Neha runs 800 m

Time = Distance / Speed

t₁ = 600/5 = 120, t₂ = 800/6 = 133.33

Ankur finishes first

Neha's distance in 120 = 6 X 120 = 720 m

Ankur wins by 800 - 720 = 80 m

Option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en: Tarun gives Hari a head-start of 60 seconds in a 2400 m race and still beats him by 40 seconds. If the speed of Hari is 6 m/s, find the speed of Tarun.
questions.solution_en:
Hari's time = 2400 / 6 = 400 s

Tarun's time = 400 - 60 - 40 = 300 s

Tarun's speed = 2400 / 300 = 8 m/s

Option (c) is the correct answer

questions.q_en: In a 1500 m race, Anil beats Bakul by 150 m and in the same race Bakul beats Charles by 75 m. By what distance does Anil beat Charles?
questions.solution_en:
Since, Anil beats Bakul by 150 m. Which means when Anil complete 1500 m, Bakul completed only 1350 m.

Also, Bakul beats Charles by 75 m. Which means when Bakul complete 1500 m, Charles completed only 1425 m.

Total distance covered by Charles when Bakul completes only 1350 m = 1425 * (1350/1500) = 1282.5 m

Hence, the distance by which Anil beats Charles = 1500 - 1282.5

= 217.5 m
